module.name: Saint Orra — Ash and Silver
module.description: Installed situations share this persistent world.

entities.name: Silver residue from the watchtower stones is carried into the spring by the kiln's forced draft; Tamsin did not poison the water.
Ys’s signed water analysis beneath the testing cup
Firing ledger: illness follows silver-stone firings, even during Tamsin's absence
Healer Ys went beneath the watchtower to recover its silver drain-key. She is alive, not hiding stolen medicine.
A charcoal flue behind the kiln enters the watchtower's undercroft, bypassing the guardian's stair.
Chalk flue survey behind the bellows
The antlered warden swore to keep grave robbers from the reservoir. Ys entered to drain it, not plunder the dead.
An oath carved into the watchtower stair
Orin Reedwalker, northern guide and trader
A dry shepherds' ledge runs from the northern track into the winter shrine, bypassing the ford.
The winter shrine's ice-pump causes the spreading frost; dismantling its exposed intake stops further growth but does not repair frozen shelters.
A salvager's account of the ice-pump and its tide marks

actions.name: Travel to {destination}
actions.report: You follow the route and arrive at the next place. People and dangers continue while you travel.

actions.name: Give {recipient} one coin
actions.report: You hand over one coin. It is now in the recipient’s purse.

actions.name: Give {recipient} one ration
actions.report: You offer a ration and step back. The recipient now owns it; what they do next is their decision.

actions.name: Eat a ration
actions.report: The company shares a ration. This satisfies hunger but does not restore health or mana.

actions.name: Collect one {goods} from {store}
actions.report: You collect one unit from the available stock. It is now carried by the company.

actions.name: Deposit one {goods} in {store}
actions.report: You deposit what the company was carrying. The stock increases and your hands are free.

actions.name: Tell {recipient}: {statement}
actions.report: You explain what the evidence establishes. The listener accepts your account and sets aside a conflicting assumption; their next choices remain their own.

actions.name: Ask {informant} about {topic}
actions.description: Ask about an offered topic. The speaker shares an established fact they actually know.
actions.report: The speaker shares an account they know. You record it in your journal.

actions.name: Destroy {witness}
actions.report: You destroy this source of evidence. Existing knowledge and other sources remain.

actions.name: Take the key for {device} from {keeper}
actions.description: Recover access from an incapacitated keeper here. You must still operate the mechanism yourself.
actions.report: You recover the keeper’s key. You can now operate the mechanism; it has not opened by itself.

actions.name: Pledge support to {recipient}
actions.description: Publicly put your name behind this person's claim.

actions.name: Disable {device}
actions.description: Dismantle an accessible mechanism you are equipped to work on. The change persists.
actions.report: You dismantle the operating mechanism. It stops; any earlier damage remains.

actions.name: Close {device}
actions.description: Close the passage this mechanism controls. People already inside can leave.
actions.report: You close the barrier. People already beyond it can leave.

actions.name: Open {device}
actions.description: Reopen the physical passage. This does not make the place beyond it safe.
actions.report: You open the barrier. The passage beyond is now available, though it may still be dangerous.

actions.name: Follow the concealed passage to {destination}
actions.report: You follow the route you learned about and emerge beyond the obstruction.

actions.name: Request passage from {keeper} as {identity}
actions.description: Invoke a company identity this keeper has explicitly agreed to honor. This is not general persuasion.
actions.report: You invoke the compact. The keeper honors your company’s standing and grants passage.

actions.name: Approach {animal} using {skill}
actions.description: Read the signals of an explicitly receptive animal and pass without provoking it. Hostile animals cannot be approached this way.
actions.report: You read the animal’s signals and approach without provoking it. The guarded route is now available.

actions.name: Have {caster} use {technique} on {recipient}
actions.description: Use a known healing or cleansing ability outside combat. Its normal mana cost is paid; combat cooldowns do not apply.
actions.report: You pause to tend a companion. The same spell effects and mana costs apply here as in battle.

actions.name: Rest and recover at {site}
actions.description: Spend six hours and one shared ration at a safe shelter. Living companions recover HP and mana; bleeding is treated. Poison and death remain. Other people and deadlines continue.
actions.report: You settle in for six hours, sharing a ration and tending your wounds. The world continues outside.

actions.name: Accept {gift} for {recipient}
actions.report: The chosen companion studies the one-use lesson. Its power is spent, but the learned ability remains available on future expeditions.

actions.name: Ask Mere what she is trying to protect
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: Mere turns the key in her hand. 'I promised these families shelter. One child is ill and Ys has vanished. I suspect Tamsin, but shutting her kiln would leave everyone cold. Show me why I am wrong: Ys left an analysis by the spring, and the kiln has a firing ledger. If they clear her, I will hear it. You can also visit the tower; I cannot order you to help.'
actions.speaker: refuge__mere

actions.name: Ask Mere what the evidence changes
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'I accused someone I should have protected,' Mere says. 'I will open the guest house and stop the draft. That costs us warmth, but I cannot keep poisoning the spring. Ys may know a way forward. Help her if you can; I cannot bring back the water we already lost.'
actions.speaker: refuge__mere

actions.name: Ask Tamsin why she stayed
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'Ys trusted me with her letter. I stayed because I thought she would come home to explain. Now they call that proof I was hiding something. Read it, or ask me about it. I want my work back without being blamed for old magic. I know how to tend a fire, not how to judge old magic.'
actions.speaker: refuge__tamsin

actions.name: Ask Ys why she risked the tower
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'Those families need clean water more than another promise. I came for the drain and could not get the siphon apart. The warden thinks everyone is a thief. Read its oath or use the flue; fighting is your choice. Open the hatch, stop the siphon and I can walk home. I have a one-use cinder seal to give you afterward. It lets one companion learn a fire invocation. It would be useful against the frost things in the northern fen.'
actions.speaker: tower__ys

actions.name: Ask Ys about tomorrow's expedition
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'We have breathing space, not a cure for every loss. The warden swore to keep grave robbers from the reservoir; I came to drain it, not plunder it. I have left a one-use cinder seal here. Let one companion study it and the invocation will be theirs permanently. Rest at the refuge before going north. Frost things hate fire, but a quiet traveler can sometimes pass them. Do not spend lives to prove you can win.'
actions.speaker: tower__ys

actions.name: Ask Ys what remains to be done
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'The seal is spent, but the invocation is part of your companion now. Take supplies and recover before going north. Stopping the frost can preserve a safe camp; taking salvage without stopping it is a different choice. I cannot promise that fighting will bring everyone home.'
actions.speaker: tower__ys

actions.name: Buy one {goods} from {merchant} for two coins
actions.description: Trade two coins for one unit from a present merchant's finite stock. This is a posted price, not a negotiation simulation.
actions.report: You pay two coins and receive one unit of supplies. The merchant's stock and both purses change accordingly.

actions.name: Recover a coin from {store}
actions.report: You recover one coin from the finite cache. It is now in the company's purse.

actions.name: Ask the guide what keeps this camp alive
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: 'Trappers, salvagers, and people who cannot afford a town bed,' the guide says. 'I have {quantity(margin__tala, rations)} rations, two coins each while my stock lasts. Pallets here are safe for recovery while the shelters stand. The wolf at the ford is changed by old cold. Fire hurts it; cold barely does. You do not have to fight. Ask me for the shepherds' route. I leave for Orra at watch {margin__departAt(margin__winter)} if the frost has not stopped.'
actions.speaker: margin__tala

actions.name: Ask for a route around the altered wolf
actions.description: Speak with someone here about an offered topic.
actions.report: The guide marks a dry ledge from the northern track to the shrine. 'You can enter without going near the ford. There is salvage beyond, but taking the money will not stop the ice-pump. You will have to choose whether to dismantle it.'
actions.speaker: margin__tala

observations.text: A barefoot child watches the testing cup beside the spring. A chalk notice blames Tamsin for the sickness; the cup covers Ys's sealed water analysis. Her note and the firing ledger can be read independently. East is the refuge porch, west the kiln, north the moor and ruined watchtower. Mere hears documented challenges. Read the analysis or the kiln ledger before accepting the accusation. The spring will be spoiled at watch 20 if firing continues.

A silver scum covers the spring. Stopping the bellows now prevents further discharge but cannot restore the stored water. The refuge's clean-water reserve has been emptied. Water collected earlier remains yours.

Mere holds the guest-house key. 'One sick child and a missing healer. I cannot risk another. I will open a hearing if you bring evidence against my judgment.' Her founding compact also admits a company of human, elf and dwarf together. Tamsin's expulsion is set for watch 28. The door is a physical barrier; if its keeper falls, you can recover her key and open it yourself; that proves nothing about the charge.

The guest-house door stands open. Tamsin can leave; Mere's decision is no longer a prison sentence. The illness and the missing healer remain separate problems. Disabling the kiln ends the discharge but also its warmth.

Tamsin sits beside a letter. 'Ys went to the tower, not away with the medicine. I promised to wait for her. Burning old stone made the glaze white; I thought it harmless.' She offers the letter freely. She cannot tell you what happened after Ys descended.
Tamsin's blanket is folded on the empty pallet. Her letter remains; a person's departure does not erase written evidence.

Bellows drive hot air through silver-flecked stones scavenged from the watchtower. You can dismantle the draft here without anyone's permission. It will stop the firing—and the refuge's heat. A ledger and flue survey lie under a loose slate. The water discharge will reach the spring at watch 20.

The dismantled bellows lie beside cold stone. No more silver ash rises toward the spring. Families huddle under blankets: removing a danger did not replace their livelihood or heat. The tower's drain still needs attention.

Tamsin has returned to her workplace after Mere accepted the evidence. The false accusation is withdrawn; the cold kiln remains a real loss. 'Find Ys. She knew how to drain the tower without firing these stones.'
Tamsin waits outside with her blanket. The expulsion happened even while you were elsewhere. Evidence can still change Mere's knowledge; it cannot erase the day Tamsin lost her shelter.

Spare pallets and a cookpot offer six hours of recovery here for one shared ration. You may stop, but the outside world will not wait. Recovery restores living companions' health and mana and treats bleeding; it does not reverse death or purge poison.

The spring runs clear and the accusation against Tamsin has been withdrawn. The refuge is colder after the kiln stopped. The northern track leads toward the trappers' camp; the watchtower still holds whatever this company has left unresolved. You can prepare at the refuge, speak to Ys if she has returned, or choose a fresh expedition.

A gaunt she-wolf stands over a den at the tower path. She watches your food, not your throat. A ranger can read her warning and pass; anyone can give her a ration and wait for her to eat. You may fight, but her death will be permanent. The green is behind you; the watchtower lies beyond her.
The path to the watchtower is passable. Beyond the broken arch, antlers scrape against stone. A low voice repeats an oath. The reservoir's tide mark is climbing toward watch 36.

Silver water has drowned the direct tower path. The collapse cannot be reversed by stopping the siphon now. The charcoal flue remains another entrance if you discovered it. The green is still reachable.

A revenant wearing a stag's skull bars the stair. 'No plunderer passes.' The oath is carved beside its hand. Ordinary weapons deal half damage to it; fire deals half again as much, radiant twice as much. It can drain life, shield itself and cast sleep resisted by wisdom. Reading and communicating its oath may establish why you came; it is not a promise that every undead creature will listen.
The warden has accepted the healer's purpose and left the stair. Its oath remains carved in stone. The reservoir is still dangerous; gaining passage did not repair it.
The antlered skull is broken. The stair is clear. No one remains here to guard the dead, and the tide continues to rise.

Ys crouches above a silver tide. 'I can open the inspection hatch. You can dismantle the siphon beyond it; I cannot abandon the patients above until this is done.' The charcoal flue leads back to the kiln. The guardian's stair leads up to the watchtower.

Silver water climbs through a narrow glass tube. Its intake brace is exposed. Dismantling the siphon prevents the reservoir overflowing at watch 36; any flooded ground stays flooded. The hatch and undercroft remain behind you.

The tube drains and the water falls below the tide marks. The reservoir has stopped climbing. Ys can return by the tower path. The stair allows anyone already below to leave; the guardian bars entry, not escape.

Ys has returned from below the watchtower. She has seen what poisoned the spring and can offer her account here. The missing-person search is over, but spoiled water, a lost kiln and dead creatures remain consequences of your history.

The northern track leaves Orra behind. A side path reaches a camp of trappers and salvagers. Beyond it the white ford leads to a ruined shrine. The guide at camp knows a way around the ford. You can return to Orra from here without entering the shrine.

Pallets surround a small cookpot. The guide sells finite rations when present; recovery here takes six hours and one shared ration. A marked route lies beside the fire. The shelters will fail at watch {margin__freezeAt(margin__winter)} if the ice-pump still runs. The guide plans to leave at watch {margin__departAt(margin__winter)}.
The guide has left. You can still use the pallets, but there is no one here to trade. Quieting the shrine before the shelters freeze can bring the guide back.
The shelters have split beneath ice. They no longer offer safe recovery. The old camp will remain damaged even if you stop the source. Orra's refuge is still reachable by the northern track.

The rime-matted wolf holds the causeway. Its cold bite can weaken a companion; its howl can stun unless resisted by wisdom. It resists physical and cold damage, but fire deals extra damage. A fire invocation from Ys can help. A guide's ledge can bypass the encounter entirely. Retreat preserves both sides' injuries.
The altered wolf lies dead. The causeway is clear. Its death has not dismantled the machine beyond it.

A bronze intake pumps silver-white cold into the ground. Its retaining pins are exposed and can be dismantled. A scattered purse lies among salvager's bones; you can take the money without repairing the shrine. The exit leads back toward the ford, and a dry ledge returns directly to the northern track.

The intake has stopped. Frost no longer advances from the shrine. Any shelter already split by ice remains ruined. The purse and the dead remain where this history left them. You can return to Orra, recover and choose another journey.
The northern guide has returned with a report: the camp's shelters split under the shrine's frost. Their supply service has moved with them; the old safe stopping place has been lost.

A northern sign points toward a trappers' camp and a winter shrine. The guide there sells rations and knows the route. Ys went beneath the watchtower to the south of that margin; you can seek her, travel north or remain at the refuge. These are choices, not orders.

installations.name: Ashes at Saint Orra: Orra frontier
installations.description: Saint Orra shelters quarry families beside a ruined watchtower. A child fell ill after drinking from the spring; the charcoal worker Tamsin is blamed. Keeper Mere has locked the guest house pending expulsion at watch 28. The kiln still warms the refuge. Investigate before lending your name to a judgment. Every action costs a watch; examining the scene never obliges you to take a side.

installations.name: The Hart Below: Orra frontier
installations.description: Above Orra's spring stands a watchtower built over a drowned burial vault. Ys the healer sought its drain-key. A hungry wolf guards the approach; a speaking revenant guards the stair. The silver-water reservoir will overflow at watch 36 unless its siphon is disabled. Neither guardian must be killed to reach it.

installations.name: The northern margin: The northern margin
installations.description: The northern camp supports trappers and salvagers beside a damaged winter shrine. The guide wants the path kept open; an altered wolf guards the old causeway. The shrine's ice-pump still draws cold into the ground. You can investigate, plunder, stop it, avoid the wolf or leave. Nothing requires a victorious fight.
